content.comment_body: Hello, Last year we installed several [product_name] controllers in our park to manage exposition lighting and gate barriers. All are programmed with the latest [product_name] software ([version_no]) and automatically switch between summer and winter time. Last weekend, the [product_name] controllers of [version_no] switched to winter time a week early, instead of at the expected time. Will the [version_no] controllers switch at the right time next weekend? Is it possible to reprogram the [version_no] controllers for the correct switching, or should we change the setting from "EU timetable" to the "self adjustable" option? Regards, [user_name] [company_name]

A workaround for the summer/winter time switching issue with [product_name] ([article_no]) controllers is to select the UK time setting instead of the EU option. The older manual for [product_name] ([article_no], page 74) available on [url] provides the correct configuration for Europe using the UK setting. This issue is improved in the newer [product_name] ([version_no]) controllers.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing unexpected time changes with earlier hardware versions of [product_name] controllers, resulting in premature switching between summer and winter schedules when using the EU timetable option. There is confusion about configuration steps and version differences, with a suggested workaround involving switching to UK regional settings. Improvement in newer hardware versions is noted, and users are seeking greater clarity and reliability for regional time management features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] controllers to reliably switch between summer and winter schedules at the correct time, with configuration options that are easy to set and consistent across hardware versions.
